startup.name: Egoist Machines
startup.one_liner: Your personal context, securely portable across every AI app.
startup.description: Egoist Machines builds AI Passport, a user controlled portable profile of the context a person generates across AI assistants and apps. Apps integrate through a sign in with AI Passport flow that requests scoped, time limited context, which users can inspect and revoke. The company built its own memory store for fast per user retrieval. Distribution is through first party consumer products and integrations into consumer apps. The long term plan is a local hardware device, Digital Domovoy, that keeps context on hardware the user controls. Two person team in San Francisco. Revenue model is not stated.

yc_acceptance.basis: The company was accepted to YC, which is the premise of this test, so the acceptance estimate is near certainty. For reference a random applicant starts near 1 percent. This team has a timely theme, privacy and AI memory, but a vague business model and a hardware ambition, so an applicant story like this would be below a typical strong B2B team on the factor table.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say no because the pitch is a platform and a protocol with no stated paying customer, a cold start network effect that needs both users and app integrators, and a hardware product years away. Partners often reject two sided identity ideas without early usage numbers, and the AI model companies are shipping their own memory features, so the wedge looked contested when applying. The acceptance step is set from the premise that the company was admitted.

ladder.why_it_fails: The likely failure is that investors cannot find a buyer. Users get little from a passport until many apps accept it and apps will not integrate until users hold passports. Meanwhile the main assistants ship their own memory import, so the consumer pain shrinks. Two founders also split attention between software and hardware. Analogs: epicenter raised only a small pre seed for a similar portable memory idea and oki likewise stayed at 500K.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series A needs a measurable network, such as many integrated apps with active passports. The most likely miss is that integrations are pilots with no usage, and consumer adoption is weak because no one sees a reason to manage a context profile. A large outcome needs the passport to become the default permission layer across AI apps, against model vendors who control the user relationship and ship memory natively.

killers.risk: Cold start network problem between users and integrating apps
killers.evidence: Value to a user depends on many apps accepting the passport and apps join only if many users hold one; no early usage is stated.
killers.mitigation: Ship a first party product that is useful alone, then open the API.

killers.risk: Model vendors ship memory and import natively
killers.evidence: Anthropic added memory import from other assistants in early 2026 and the assistants already keep their own memory.
killers.mitigation: Be the neutral layer for apps outside the big assistants.

killers.risk: No clear payer or business model
killers.evidence: The description names no customer who pays and consumer privacy products historically monetize poorly.
killers.mitigation: Charge apps per verified context request.

killers.risk: Hardware ambition splits a two person team
killers.evidence: Digital Domovoy needs hardware design, supply chain and capital that two founders cannot cover while building software.
killers.mitigation: Defer hardware until the software layer has usage.

technical_complexity.rationale: A scoped permission layer and fast per user memory retrieval are doable by a strong small team. The hard parts are getting access to context held by other apps, secure on device processing, and any hardware, which two people cannot finish in three months.

takeover_risk.rationale: The big assistants already offer memory and import tools and control sign in. They have the distribution and incentive to keep context inside their own products, so a neutral layer depends on their cooperation or on a niche they ignore.

evidence.claim: Users and commentators describe AI memory as trapped in each vendor, and guides exist for moving it between assistants.
Memory infrastructure companies are raising money, such as a 20M Series A for a memory layer.

roadmap.goal: Prove that people keep a passport and apps request it.
actions: Ship a first party product that people use daily.
Sign five consumer apps to the sign in flow with live traffic.
roadmap.proof: Weekly active passports and requests per app growing for eight weeks

roadmap.goal: Show a repeatable integration and revenue model.
actions: Price scoped context access per request or per active user.
Hit retention above 40 percent at three months on holders.

pros.evidence: Memory layer companies from recent YC batches raised seeds and an A.

pros.point: Privacy and user ownership is a clear differentiator from the assistants
pros.evidence: The pitch is explicitly user governed access with revocation, which assistants have little incentive to build.

narrative.headline: A timely idea with a hard cold start and a crowded memory field, likely to stop at seed.
narrative.general_summary: Egoist Machines wants a portable, user controlled context layer across AI apps. Memory is a hot theme and peer YC companies have raised, so a seed above the YC check is a coin flip rather than a long shot. Beyond that, the passport needs both users and integrating apps, the model vendors are building memory and import themselves, and the business model is unstated. Hardware adds cost and delay. The ladder sits slightly under the cohort anchors, with the highest chance of ending as a stalled product or a small acquihire.
